Integration of the landing-site dependency bump: landing/package.json line 13 moves next 16.2.6 to 16.4.1, and landing/package-lock.json is regenerated. The replayed patch shows next at 16.4.1 with @next/env and the @next/swc-* packages at 16.4.1. Nested postcss moves 8.4.31 to 8.5.23, with nanoid, source-map-js, baseline-browser-mapping, undici (dev-only) and sharp 0.34.5 to 0.35.5 (libvips 1.3.4) also updated. Every replayed entry keeps a registry.npmjs.org resolved URL and a sha512 integrity value. I saw no git, http, file or alternate-registry sources and no removed integrity fields. sharp drops hasInstallScript, which slightly reduces install-time script exposure. The sharp Node engine floor is now >=20.9.0, matching next's existing floor; this is a build compatibility matter, not a security one. next's dependency declarations in the lock (@next/env 16.4.1, @swc/helpers 0.5.23, sharp ^0.35.5) are consistent with the package.json bump.

The landing site is a marketing frontend. It is outside the in-scope components (provider, native runtime, coordinator WebSocket contract, keys, attestation, fan helper). It touches none of the assets A-001..A-018 or boundaries TB-002/003/007/009/010/011/012, and none of the T-xxx threats, including T-041.

Coverage limits: the integration replay is incomplete (13 units omitted), and the supplied patches are truncated. I could not verify integrity hashes against the registry or inspect the upstream release contents. @next/eslint-plugin-next stays at 16.2.6, a non-security version mismatch in package.json. These are unverified supply-chain contracts, not evidence of a regression, so I report no findings.
